theater: 朝鮮半島西部與遼東南部

battle.name: 古朝鮮-燕國戰爭
battle.theater: 朝鮮半島西部與遼東南部
battle.brief: 《三國史記·東萊紀》載，前三〇〇年燕太子丹自朝鮮歸燕，勸燕昭王伐純王，燕軍大舉東來，破朝鮮城邑、追純王至釜山，買童則以卑沙城萬人拒敵而死。卡面這支早王朝青銅長矛，正對應傳記中以刀矛為事的朝鮮部眾與燕軍步卒：矛是青銅時代守城與野戰的基本兵器，卻換不回盾陣的厚度與步列的秩序。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 《三國史記·東萊紀》記載的那一場戰爭，交手的是北方燕國與半島上的朝鮮政權。燕國正值戰國後期，都城在薊，國君昭王在位三十三年，前二八四年遣大將軍樂毅出師，一舉攻破齊國七十餘城，把齊地變成燕國的後方；燕軍以步兵、弩手與車騎混編的方陣作戰，攻城講究圍城與突擊並用，短兵相接的一線仍由矛、戈、劍與大盾扛住。朝鮮一方並非編制嚴整的中央王國，而是王庭加上沿海地方勢力拼成的邦國：辰王在位時曾厚待燕國太子丹，把這位質子留在王都；辰王死後純王繼位，漁戶出身的滿腹、買童父子手中卻握有能夠築城列陣的武裝，買童招募亡命者達萬人，在萊州海濱築起卑沙城。純王朝廷能直接調度的兵源遠不如燕，卻握有地利與熟悉的海岸；燕國投入的是遠道而來的攻勢大軍，朝鮮投入的是守城民兵與地方豪強的私兵。兩邊的指揮系統因此極不對稱：燕王在薊城策應，統籌大軍與糧道，朝鮮的決策卻分散在王都、卑沙城與各座城邑之間，一遇敗績就各自退守。
countriesEn: The conflict recorded in the Dongnae chronicle of the Samguk Sagi was fought between the northern state of Yan and a Korean polity on the peninsula. Yan sat at the height of the late Warring States period, its capital at Ji, its king Zhao ruling thirty-three years; in 284 BC he sent the general Yue Yi out, and the army took more than seventy cities of Qi in a single stroke, turning Qi into Yan's rear base. Yan fielded mixed formations of foot, crossbowmen, chariots and cavalry, and when a city was taken they combined siege with sudden assault, while the shock of close combat still fell to spear, ge, sword and large shield. The Korean side was not a tightly organised central kingdom but a confederation assembled from the royal court and local coastal powers: in the reign of King Cheon the Yan prince Dan was treated generously and kept at the royal capital as a hostage; after Cheon died his son King Jun succeeded, yet Manbok and their son Manjung, who came from a fishing family, controlled arms capable of building walls and deploying in formation. Manjung gathered ten thousand runaways and raised the fortress of Pisa on the coast of Lai Province. The royal court could not muster the men that Yan could, but it held the ground and knew the coast; Yan brought a mobile army of invasion from far away, Korea brought militia and the private retainers of local magnates. The two command systems were therefore badly asymmetric: the Yan king directed everything from Ji, coordinating the army and the grain route, while Korean decisions were split between the capital, Pisa and the individual city walls, so a single defeat sent every place back into its own defensive shell.
people: 關鍵人物集中在三處。燕國的決策者是國君昭王與太子丹：丹本是燕國太子，早年被送往朝鮮當質子，在那裡與辰王相善，辰王死後他奔喪而歸，回到燕國便向昭王力言純王年幼、其國可取，於是有了這場東征；後來他流亡到秦國，以督亢地圖行刺秦王，事載《史記·刺客列傳》。朝鮮王庭的主角是純王，前三年曾以執送太子丹為條件換取燕軍暫退，其人在傳記中顯得進退失據；真正擋住燕軍腳步的是買童，他築卑沙城、聚萬人抗敵，最後與城俱歿，其父滿腹是這支部武裝的發起人。旁觀者亦有份：樂毅在十餘年前已為燕軍開過破齊的先例，示範了長距離攻勢可以走多遠；秦國在背後既是燕人膽怯的來源，也是丹最後落腳的去處。辰王的厚道與純王的被迫應對同樣是關鍵：朝鮮對質子的兩種處置，正說明王權與地方勢力之間沒有穩定的秩序。漢家文獻把同一個人記成兩個樣子——《史記·蘇秦列傳》另記燕太子丹曾質於齊——也讓這場戰爭的主角至今無法完全坐實。
peopleEn: The decisive figures stand in three groups. In Yan there was the king Zhao and his heir Dan: Dan had been sent to Korea as a hostage while still young, had been on good terms with King Cheon there, and after the king's death he came to mourn and went home, where he pressed the argument before Zhao that Jun was a boy and his state could be taken; that counsel began the eastern campaign. Dan later fled to Qin and attempted the assassination of the Qin king with the map of Dangkou, an episode preserved in the Records of the Historian's biography of the assassins. In the Korean court the central figure was King Jun, who in his first years had halted the Yan army by handing over Prince Dan as a hostage of his own, and who appears in the chronicle as a ruler pushed into impossible choices. The man who actually held the Yan army at bay was Manjung, who built the fortress of Pisa, gathered ten thousand men to defend it and was buried with the walls; his father Manbok was the founder of that armed following. Bystanders mattered too: Yue Yi had shown a decade earlier how deep a long offensive march could be carried, and Qin was at once the source of Yan's fear and the place where Dan finally ended up. Cheon's generosity and Jun's enforced responses matter in the same way: Korea's two dealings with one hostage show that no settled order existed between the royal court and the local powers. Chinese documents even record the same man in two different guises — the Shiji biography of Su Qin has a Yan prince Dan held as a hostage at Qi — which is why not one actor in this war can be pinned down completely.
kits: 兵器部分要從傳記的零星字句推開。朝鮮部眾的近戰手段，據《三國志·魏書·東夷傳》對樂浪、帶方居民的概括，離不開刀與矛，再加弓矢；與朝鮮同時代的青銅器考古材料中，矛頭是最常見的近戰器形之一，銅質矛頭安在木杆上，與木盾、獸皮或魚皮製的甲衣配用，弓以木與角製，箭鏃為石或骨。燕軍則是典型戰國裝備：柳葉形銅劍、刺盾用的雙股殳、數十斤重的長矛、大盾、弩與機關弩，攻城尚有雲梯一類的器械。卡面那支埃及長矛屬早王朝時期，銅或青銅矛頭纏綁於木杆，埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地——它的價值在於說明一件武器可以跨兩千六百年不變形制：矛是最早普及、也最容易在戰場上補充的冷兵器，成敗取決於拿矛的人是否排成了能被保護的隊形。傳記裡買童的萬人守城、燕軍的攻城序列，用的正是這類最耐用的近戰兵器：矛不決定勝負，卻決定城牆失守之後還有多少人站得住。
kitsEn: On arms the chronicle offers only fragments, and the rest has to be reconstructed from archaeology and parallel states. The close combat of the Korean population is summarised, in the Wei shu account of the Eastern Barbarians, by the knife and the spear, backed by the bow; among the bronze finds contemporary with Korea, spearheads are among the commonest close combat forms, a bronze blade socketed or lashed to a wooden shaft and used with wooden shields and leather or fish-skin armour, while bows were of wood and horn with stone or bone arrowheads. A Yan army on the other hand carried the standard late Warring States kit: leaf-shaped bronze swords, the double-pointed shu used for catching shields, heavy spears of many tens of jin, large shields, crossbows and repeating crossbows, plus siege ladders for the walls. The spear on this card belongs to the Egyptian Early Dynastic period, a copper or bronze head bound onto a wooden shaft; the Egyptians used it to hold city walls and later to win back lost ground. Its point is to show that a weapon can keep one shape across twenty-six centuries. The spear was the earliest and most easily replaced arm on the battlefield, and the outcome depended less on the weapon than on whether the men who carried it stood in a line that could be protected. The ten thousand who held Pisa in the chronicle and the siege columns of Yan were armed with exactly such durable close combat weapons: the spear did not decide the battle, but it decided how many men were still standing after the wall had fallen.
tactics: 燕軍自薊出發，沿遼東走廊南下，最後一段必須翻越山嶺、橫渡半島北部的諸條河川，糧道要靠車運與徵發沿途粟米、逐站屯積，這就決定了它的戰法必須快：前鋒銜接、圍城拔城、留兵守城、主力前推，而不是遠離糧道去曠野裡求決戰。攻城需要器械與時間，燕人便以連續拔城的方式把戰果滾動向前，兵鋒所至，糧秣與器械跟著向前，攻城即是取糧。朝鮮方面的戰術完全相反：兵力集中於要點，以卑沙城這樣的依山面海之城死守，買童的萬人不出城野戰，只以弓矢與長矛封住進攻者的接近；純王在野戰失利後向海邊退，把燕軍拖進丘陵與潮間帶，同時以交出質子、割地議和拖延對方。買童守城還有一層本事：他不與燕軍在開闊地帶決戰，而是讓進攻者必須逐段接近，人在城下會失去陣形，弓矢的射程卻屬守方。燕軍若留下守城就分兵，若不留下就會被空城牽制，這是進攻方在遠離本土時最典型的兩難，也是傳記中燕軍始終無法把戰果變成佔領的原因。
tacticsEn: The Yan army left Ji and moved down the Liao-dong corridor, and in its final stretch it had to cross hills and the rivers of the northern peninsula; grain had to travel by cart and be gathered and stored stage by stage along the way, so its method had to be fast: spearhead units in contact, one city after another taken, garrisons left behind, the main body pressed forward, rather than a long march away from the supply route to seek a decision in the open field. Siege needed engines and hours, so the Yan method was to roll the results forward from one captured city to the next, the army's own food and equipment moving with it, taking a city being the same thing as taking grain. Korean tactics were the mirror image. Strength was concentrated at decisive points and held in dead-defence cities such as Pisa, which stood with the mountains behind and the sea in front; Manjung's ten thousand did not meet the attacker in the open but shut the approach with arrows and long spears. There was a further skill in Manjung's defence: he refused to be drawn into a set-piece battle in open ground, forcing the attacker to advance in stages, because men lose their formation under a wall while the range of the bow belongs to the defenders. After the defeat in the field, King Jun fell back towards the coast, drawing the Yan columns into hills and tidal flats while buying time with the offer of a hostage and a negotiated surrender. The besiegers were caught between leaving garrisons behind, which split their force, and leaving cities in their rear, which left them open.
data: 數字方面，傳記留下的極少，但可核者仍有幾條。斷代按《三國史記》的紀年，純王三年對應公元前三〇〇年，這也是中文戰爭列表採用該年的依據；燕昭王的在位期是前311年至前279年，戰役落在其晚年攻勢的頂點。傳記記買童招集亡命者「萬人」築卑沙城，這是唯一明確的兵力數字；燕軍的數目則沒有留下可核的記載，只以「大舉」形容。可作旁證的是：前二八四年燕軍一舉破齊七十餘城，可見其攻城能力與兵源在當時列國中屬上乘；但自薊至萊州一線，直線距離在一千公里以上，遠征補給的負擔自此決定戰役規模；前二七九年田單復齊，燕控制的齊地人心未定，也限制其再抽調兵力的餘裕。史料對照同樣重要：《史記·燕世家》記燕昭王的用兵有伐齊、逐北狄、築長城，獨無伐朝鮮之戰；《史記·刺客列傳》記太子丹刺秦在公元前二二七年，與前300年已隔七十三年，若視為同一人則年代難以並存。中原同期史料的沉默，正是這場戰爭至今仍有爭議的原因。
dataEn: Numbers are scarce in the chronicle, but a few can be checked. Under the chronology of the Samguk Sagi the third year of King Jun corresponds to 300 BC, and that is the year taken by the Chinese list of wars. Zhao's reign ran from 311 to 279 BC, so the campaign fell in the late, high point of his offensive. The chronicle records Manjung gathering ten thousand men to raise Pisa, and that is the only explicit figure it gives; the size of the Yan army is not stated, and the text describes only a great expedition. Supporting evidence points the same way: in 284 BC the Yan army took more than seventy cities of Qi in one campaign, which places its siege capacity and manpower among the best of the age, but the straight line from Ji to the Lai coast runs well over a thousand kilometres, and the burden of a distant supply line from that moment set the scale of the whole operation; in 279 BC Tian Dan restored Qi, and the unrest of the occupied Qi land further limited how many troops Yan could detach. The silence of the Chinese sources matters as much: the Shiji chronicle of Yan records campaigns against Qi, the northern tribes and long-wall building, but no war against Korea, and the Shiji assassination narrative places Dan's attempt in 227 BC, seventy-three years after 300 BC, so the two cannot belong to the same man on one chronology. That silence is why the dating of this war is still disputed.
cause: 起事的原因，傳記給了最直接的一條：燕太子丹自朝鮮歸國，向昭王陳說純王幼弱、國可取，於是燕王起兵。往深一層看，前三百年華北的秩序正在崩解：秦已滅韓、趙、魏，逼近燕境，昭王一面卑辭事秦、一面倚齊地以自厚，急需在東北方向取得可以養兵的廣地與屏障；破齊之後的燕國正處國力頂點，也需要一個能被迅速拿下、又不算深入中原腹心的地方來消化兵勢。朝鮮這邊也有裂縫：辰王厚待質子的做法與純王對地方武裝的依賴並存，買童以海民首領之身築城擁兵，本身就是對王權的半獨立，內部的消息傳到燕國，變成了可乘之機。質子外交本來是燕國在東北亞伸手的常規手段，東胡、樓煩與齊國都曾收留燕人，朝鮮卻把丹待得太好，好到燕國無法再把這裡當作可以隨時索取的籌碼。於是同一場戰爭有兩重動力：燕國要的是地理與榮譽，朝鮮的邊緣勢力要的是不被王都吞併。
causeEn: The chronicle gives one direct cause: Prince Dan returned from Korea and told Zhao that Jun was young and his state could be taken, and the king raised an army. Underneath that, the order of northern China was breaking down in the third century BC. Qin had already destroyed Han, Zhao and Wei and was pressing towards Yan's borders; Zhao humoured Qin while leaning on the Qi lands he had taken, and he needed new ground to the north-east on which to feed troops and to build a screen. Yan after the conquest of Qi stood at the peak of its strength and wanted a place that could be taken quickly without marching deep into the heartland of China. Korea had cracks of its own. The generous treatment of the hostage under Cheon sat uneasily with Jun's dependence on local armed men, and Manjung, a sea-side chief who raised walls and troops, was himself a semi-independent rival to the court; word of this internal weakness reached Yan and became the opening it wanted. Hostage diplomacy was a normal instrument for Yan in Northeast Asia — the Donghu, Loufan and Qi had all once sheltered Yan men — but Korea treated Dan so well that Yan could no longer treat the place as something it could call in at will. Two motives therefore pushed the same war forward: Yan wanted territory and prestige, and Korea's peripheral power wanted not to be swallowed by the capital.
impact: 若照傳記的敘事走完，這場戰爭留下的不是疆界，而是兩個長遠的問題。第一個是朝鮮在東北亞的位置：從此它在東方文獻裡不再只是半島上的邊裔政權，而是被中原諸侯當作棋子和屬國看待的一環；買童戰死、卑沙城陷落之後，朝鮮政權被迫重整，純王得以保住王位，其後的統治重心緩慢移向帶方一帶，漢代樂浪、帶方等郡的格局，可以看成一條更長的線的末端。第二個是歷史敘述本身：「古朝鮮」是否曾是一個連貫的中國古代王朝，韓國學界以李光順、宮本延人等為代表，多半持否定或保留態度，認為傳記的年代層次混雜、難與出土資料對應；中國學界則傾向把它讀作早期中原王朝經營東北的開端。前三〇八年漢武帝滅朝鮮、設四郡，則把「朝鮮」從國名變成郡名，《山海經·海內經》更早就把這個名字列在東方之國的序列裡。兵器史的旁證也很清楚：從埃及早王朝的青銅矛到戰國的長矛，形制跨越三千年幾乎未變，說明左右戰局的是兵源的組織與補給，而不是武器本身。
impactEn: If the chronicle's narrative is followed through, this war left behind no frontier but two long questions. The first is Korea's place in Northeast Asia: from this point it was no longer merely a frontier polity on the peninsula in the eastern texts, but a piece and a client of the Chinese states. After Manjung's death and the fall of Pisa, the Korean polity had to reorganise, Jun kept his throne, and the centre of gravity slowly shifted towards the Daifang region; the Han commanderies of Lelang and Daifang are the far end of that longer line. The second question is historical narrative itself. Whether Gojoseon was ever a continuous Chinese dynasty is disputed: Korean scholars such as Lee Kwang-soon and Miyanaka Nobuhito tend to reject or heavily qualify the idea, pointing to the mixed chronological layers of the chronicle and its poor fit with excavated material, while Chinese scholarship tends to read it as the opening of early Chinese engagement with the Northeast. In 108 BC the Han destroyed Korea and set up four commanderies, turning a state name into an administrative one, and the Shanhai Jing had already listed the name among the states of the east. The arms history adds a parallel: from the Egyptian Early Dynastic bronze spear to the Warring States spear the form barely changes across three millennia, showing that organisation and supply decided the battle, not the weapon.
result: 傳記的結局是打了又撤。頭一輪進攻純王兵敗，收攏殘兵後他做了一件在外交上極不尋常的事：把太子丹送去做燕國的人質，用這個人換回暫時的罷兵；到了純王三年，燕軍再舉大兵，一度在傳記所記的釜山擊破純王，接連攻下沿海岸的城邑，純王退保海邊；這時買童以卑沙城的萬人出來拒敵，而雙方的目標恰好指向相反的方向：燕軍需要一個可以長久據守的落腳點，朝鮮則需要把進攻者拖到不能久待的距離。買童死、卑沙城破，傳記的敘述就此收束——燕軍沒有留下永久據點，沒有改變朝鮮政權的性質，也沒有解決純王的王位；戰役之後雙方回到以質子維繫的舊關係，朝鮮在名義上仍算獨立於漢，直到前108年才被漢朝直接置郡。勝利者並沒有收穫戰果：燕國自己也只多撐了不足八十年，前222年終為秦所滅。這或許是最能說明這場戰爭性質的結局。
resultEn: The chronicle ends with a war fought and then withdrawn. In the first round of attacks King Jun was beaten; gathering what was left of his forces he did something diplomatically unusual, sending Prince Dan to Yan as a hostage of his own and buying a temporary halt with the man. In the third year of Jun, Yan marched again in force, defeated Jun at the place the chronicle calls Busan, took city after city along the coast, and the king fell back towards the sea. At that point Manjung came out of Pisa with his ten thousand to meet them, and the two sets of objectives pulled in opposite directions: Yan needed a foothold it could hold permanently, while Korea needed to drag the attacker out to a distance it could not outlast. Manjung died and Pisa fell, and there the chronicle stops. The Yan army left no permanent base, changed nothing in the nature of the Korean polity and did not settle the question of Jun's throne; afterwards both sides fell back on the old arrangement of hostages, and Korea remained independent in name until the Han commanderies of 108 BC. The victor harvested nothing: Yan itself survived less than eighty years more and was destroyed by Qin in 222 BC. That is perhaps the most telling outcome of all.
